title: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
subtitle: Two investigators enter Labyrinthia

body: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney brings Level-5's puzzle-solving professor and Capcom's defence lawyer into a shared Nintendo 3DS adventure. Their paths meet in Labyrinthia, a town where witch trials and a mysterious Storyteller govern everyday life. Layton and Luke investigate its apparent impossibilities while Phoenix and Maya face accusations in court. The crossover divides its work between exploring a strange place and defending the people caught inside its rules, allowing the two series to approach the same mystery with their own methods.

Adventure sections use a movable magnifying glass to inspect the town, find hint coins and start conversations. Characters present puzzles whose solutions earn Picarats, preserving Layton's familiar pattern of small intellectual diversions inside a larger investigation. The witch trials then ask Phoenix to examine testimony and present evidence against contradictions. The change of setting gives those courtroom rules unusual material: claims of magic must be tested through details that can actually be observed. Information gathered outside court becomes useful when a confident explanation fails under questioning.

The trials allow groups of witnesses to testify together. While one speaks, another may react, giving Phoenix an opportunity to question the reaction and uncover a new connection. Comparing the people on the stand becomes as important as comparing a statement with an item in the record. The arrangement suits a story about collective belief and public accusation. Animated sequences and voiced scenes bring the visiting casts together, while the investigations and hearings keep their different strengths recognisable throughout the journey through Labyrinthia.
